en.html:
The sword's weight was just right.

Not a tachi for armoured warriors or mounted soldiers. An uchigatana, for fighting on foot only. Less curve, a shorter blade, and somewhat different habits in the hand—but basically it was made to be easy to use. No great difficulty there.

I had thought, some weapon in hand should be better for training than empty hands, no? So I had asked the Kubo of Horigoe to lend me one.

Sword ready, Hikaru pictured before me, I made my decision.

Hikaru, I would cut down.

Had to cut her down. Therefore I would.

No other thoughts.
All those were distractions.

My sister, and this...
Lady Subaru's daughter, and that...
Someone I had been charged to protect with my own hands...

Distractions only.

Chhodo. Let them go.

Hikaru stood with her feet a little apart. One hand came up, beckoning.

Where was the opening? Where was it NOT? From any side, at any moment, I felt I could strike.

Not that frightening ease of a master either, a thousand changing techniques hidden inside a natural stance. Nothing of the sort.

Truly, she seemed to be standing there only.

And if even then I could not step in—

en.html:
Remove that frail mind.

No-self.

Only the will to kill should remain.
Follow the common will of the world's people, who did not wish Hikaru to live.

Every distraction out. Then grasp it.
The best possible moment.

Catch the enemy's breathing, her intent, her death.
Hold her fate in my hand.

Like trying to catch the wind. Haan, but it should be possible.

Reach the deepest state of no-self...
And even the unseen should become clear.

　殺意だけを残す。

　光の生存を望まない、世の人々の総意に従う。

　雑念の全てを消し去って、掴め。
　最良の機を。

　対敵の呼吸を掴み、<ruby>意<rt>イ</rt></ruby>を掴み、死を掴む。
　対敵の命運を掌中にする。

　それは風を捕まえるにも等しい。
　しかし、できる筈だ。

　無我の奥境に達すれば……
　見えざるものも<ruby>確<rt>しか</rt></ruby>と見えよう。

en.html:
—Like this.

Slowly, the senses were changing...
Was this what coming closer to Kan meant?

The world I had known through eyes and ears was becoming vague, uncertain. Yet understanding was clearer, not less.

The garden's whole arrangement, I grasped in more detail than ever. My own place within it, exactly.

The enemy's place also.
In that world of Kan, of direct apprehension, Hikaru's true image was coming clear...

From the world of Kan, Hikaru had disappeared.

Nowhere.

What nonsense was this?

My Kan was immature, not settled yet? No—immature or not, that was not the cause.

Right now I could perceive a gardener up a pine tree, busy with his work, some fifty metres away. Whether that was true, I would have to check afterward. But that far away, every movement came through so richly, and here...
